classification.difficultyReason: Identify positive skewness and compare the spread of distributions on matching scales.

content.prompt: Which of these graphs best represents positively skewed data with the smaller standard deviation?

spec.description: Four horizontally aligned qualitative distribution graphs labelled A, B, C and D in bold uppercase. All have matching horizontal ranges, arrowed axes and endpoint labels 0 and 100. Curves are editable qualitative reconstructions; no numerical density function is asserted.
spec.mathematics: A and C have right tails and are positively skewed. C is more concentrated than A. B and D have left tails.
spec.answerVisibility: All four choices are permanent student-visible givens; no answer is marked.

answer.worked: A and C are positively skewed because their tails extend to the right. C has less spread than A, so it has the smaller standard deviation. Correct answer: C.
